observation.evaluation:
Correctness: PARTIALLY_CORRECT
Safety: CAUTION
Issues: The lateral image can show pleural effusion (e.g., posterior costophrenic sulcus blunting) but cannot reliably lateralize it to right versus left; the “L” marker is an orientation/projection marker, not evidence that the effusion is on the left or right; the risk text itself acknowledges that a single lateral view cannot definitively lateralize, so selecting B is not supported by the image alone; model consensus is not image evidence.
Suggestion: Confirm laterality with a frontal radiograph or ultrasound before assigning right versus left pleural effusion; do not use the L marker as evidence of the effusion side.
